conflicts: Level energies: 25 099.8(2) / 25 111.8(2) cm^-1 (255Fm, buffer gas, 2003) vs 25 099.760(14) / 25 111.760(12) cm^-1 (255Fm, vacuum, 2026); they agree, the 2026 values are entered. Warbinek et al. 2024 print 25 111.75(2) for 255Fm on their gas-cell scale (pressure shift included).

Partial rates of the two 398 nm lines: the thesis gives 3.6(7) and 3.6(6) x 10^6 /s; Allehabi et al. 2020 quote (3.4 +- 0.8) and (3.5 +- 0.7) x 10^6 /s from the published papers (not opened). Thesis values entered, quoted ones under alternatives.

Hyperfine constants of 255Fm: the 2005 values (two interpretations of an unresolved spectrum, e.g. ground state A = -320 or -760 MHz, B = -22 000 or -8 700 MHz) disagree with the 2026 resolved measurement (A = -149.5(1.1), B = -10 460(40) MHz); the 2026 authors state their result revises the earlier data. For the R2 level the second 2005 interpretation is quoted with B = +0.39 GHz (2026 paper) and -390 MHz (Allehabi 2020). The two printings of the 2026 paper quote different 2005 sets in Table I: the journal version (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 192501) prints the second interpretation (A = -0.76 / -0.66 / -0.73 GHz, B = -8.7 / -14.8 / +0.39 GHz), the preprint arXiv:2511.20921v1 prints the first (A = -0.32 / -0.53 / -0.69 GHz, B = -22 / -2.9 / -1.7 GHz); the caption's 'error of 50 %' applies to whichever set is shown. The new measured constants are identical in both printings.
J of the 25 111.8 cm^-1 level: the thesis abstract writes the proposed term as 5G6 while its Table 7.2 and text give 5G J = 5; J = 5 is confirmed by the 2026 hyperfine fit.
255Fm magnetic moment: -0.743(49) mu_N in Table III and -0.75(5) mu_N in the abstract of the 2026 paper (rounding).

Calculated order of the two J = 6 / J = 5 levels near 25 100 cm^-1 and their theoretical energies differ between Allehabi 2020 (25 442, 25 494) and Dzuba 2023 (25 468, 25 542); both assign R1 to J = 6 and R2 to J = 5.

Ionization energy: autoionizing states used as ionization steps are reported at 52 077.2, 52 081.4 (2026) and 52 166 cm^-1 (2024), below the NIST bracketed limit 52 400(600) and below the central surface-ionization value 6.52(13) eV = 52 590(1050) cm^-1 (both still compatible within their uncertainties). If these states do autoionize, the limit lies below about 52 077 cm^-1 (derived remark, not a published result).

notes: NIST lists only the ground level and a bracketed (extrapolated) limit. Seven odd levels are known, all found by resonance ionization of 255Fm from the ground state: two near 398 nm (R1, R2; energies, J and hyperfine constants from the 2026 high-resolution work, entered as measured) and five between 365 and 352 nm (2005, second-hand, +-1.5 cm^-1, J from theory). A_s of the two 398 nm lines are partial rates from saturation measurements (model-dependent); A_s of the other five lines and all g_J are calculated values marked theory; A_s_lower_bound holds the two measured lower limits. No lifetime is stored. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second), reference 250Fm, on the R2 line. Hyperfine constants were printed in GHz and converted to MHz. Term labels of the excited levels are leading components of calculated wavefunctions (proposals). The broad structure at 25 740(5) cm^-1 seen in 2003 (about 30 cm^-1 wide, possibly a two-photon resonance) is not entered as a level. CLAUDE.md of the project records an earlier owner decision not to add Fm; this file was written at the request of the 2026-10-02 workflow task and changes nothing else.
